stem: For a publication figure with colored gates, saved as a high-resolution PNG via `savefig`, which `draw()` output fits?

options.text: `output="mpl"` — returns a Matplotlib `Figure`, typically styled and then written out with `savefig`.
`output="text"` — returns ASCII art, ideal for quick inspection in a terminal.
`output="latex_source"` — a LaTeX string, not a high-resolution image.
the default `draw()` with no argument — gives you the same ASCII text drawing.
`output="latex"` — the high-resolution renderer; typically returns a Matplotlib `Figure` for `savefig`.

explanation.correct: The `mpl` renderer returns a `matplotlib.figure.Figure`, which supports colored gate boxes, style customization, and `fig.savefig(...)` to any raster or vector format. That is exactly what a publication-quality circuit figure needs.

distractors.B: The text renderer produces monochrome ASCII intended for terminals and logs; it cannot make colored boxes or a savable raster image.
distractors.C: `latex_source` returns a LaTeX string you would still have to compile yourself; it is not a ready-to-save high-resolution image and offers no Matplotlib styling.
distractors.D: With no argument `draw()` defaults to the text (ASCII) renderer — the opposite of the styleable, high-resolution figure you want.
distractors.E: The docs do call `latex` output "high-quality images", but that renderer needs an external LaTeX toolchain and returns a PIL `Image`, not a Matplotlib `Figure`: it has `save`, no `savefig`, and no Matplotlib style hook for tuning the drawing.
